source_scope: two edited historical sources and one peer-reviewed research article, selected sections

sources.author: Carlos de Sigüenza y Góngora
sources.title: Alboroto y motín de México del 8 de junio de 1692
sources.edition: Relaciones históricas, UNAM 1992 edition, printed pp.81–151
sources.examined: selected text pp.110–112, 124–131; modern edition of contemporary eyewitness narrative; manuscript not inspected

sources.title: Actas del Cabildo de la Ciudad de México, 1692 (edited chronological abstracts)
sources.publisher: Biblioteca Francisco Xavier Clavigero, Universidad Iberoamericana
sources.examined: PDF pp.1–3; editorial abstracts of 16 June through 4 July acts, not archival facsimiles

sources.author: Arnaud Exbalin
sources.title: Riot in Mexico City: a challenge to the colonial order?
sources.examined: HTML text sections The riot as expression of urban government in crisis; Weakness of forces of law and order; Restoring order

findings.subject: Food procurement before the riot
findings.assertion: In a 29 April 1692 consultation, viceregal authorities allowed broad trading in maize and wheat while trying to secure maize already arranged from Celaya, Toluca and Chalco; Sigüenza later described late-May shortages when the expected shipments lagged.
findings.exact_locator: printed pp.110–112; 29 April grain consultation; last week of May
findings.limitations: Sigüenza praises the viceroy; his account of the causes and legality of purchases is partisan.

findings.subject: Women supplying stones in the Plaza Mayor
findings.assertion: At about 6:30 p.m. on 8 June, eyewitness Sigüenza says Indigenous women supplied stones to people attacking the viceregal palace; his account also describes participants including Indigenous people, Black and mixed-ancestry residents.
findings.exact_locator: printed pp.128–129; eyewitness begins at 'A nada... me hallé presente'
findings.limitations: Witness observed only a portion of the riot and uses overtly contemptuous language about the urban poor.

findings.subject: Movement between institutions during the riot
findings.assertion: Exbalin reconstructs protesters seeking the corregidor, then the archbishop, and finally the viceroy before destructive attacks on the buildings around the central plaza.
findings.exact_locator: section 'The riot as the expression of an urban government in crisis', Figure 1 and paragraphs on the protesters' trajectory
findings.limitations: Sequence is historian's reconstruction from Sigüenza, Robles and later scholarship; exact movements and the alleged dead woman are contested.

findings.subject: Disruption of city-government premises
findings.assertion: The cabildo abstract dated 16 June 1692 records damage from the 8 June uprising and orders repair of the Alhóndiga, temporary use of the pósito room for council meetings, and return of capitular books held by Sigüenza.
findings.exact_locator: edited cabildo abstract, PDF p.1, meeting 16 June 1692
findings.limitations: Only an editorial summary inspected; surviving original municipal minutes not inspected.

findings.subject: Thirteen canoes of maize from Chalco
findings.assertion: A 26 June 1692 council abstract records councilor Juan de Aguirre's report that, on viceregal orders, he obtained and forwarded thirteen canoes of maize from Chalco to Mexico City.
findings.exact_locator: edited cabildo abstract, PDF p.1, 26 June, 'TESTIMONIO DEL REGIDOR AGUIRRE'
findings.limitations: Aguirre's retrospective self-report, mediated by an editorial abstract; no independent measurement or delivery receipt checked.

findings.subject: Indigenous neighborhood officials in grain distribution plan
findings.assertion: On 27 June 1692, the city council proposed allocating a share of daily maize deliveries to governors of San Juan and Santiago and other neighborhood leaders to distribute to Indigenous families alongside parish ministers.
findings.exact_locator: edited cabildo abstract, PDF p.2, 27 June, 'DISPENDIO DE MAÍCES'
findings.limitations: Proposed consultation with viceroy; does not prove the distribution system was implemented.

findings.subject: Vaulted market stalls proposed after the fire
findings.assertion: A 26 June council proposal sought two rows of lime-and-stone vaulted market stalls with iron-faced doors around Plaza Mayor; a 4 July abstract reports viceregal approval and instruction to master builder Cristóbal de Molina Vargas to draft the plan.
findings.exact_locator: edited abstracts, PDF pp.2–3, 26 June and 4 July 1692
findings.limitations: Approval of design is not proof that these specific stalls were constructed or survive today.

findings.subject: Damaged public archives and rescued paintings
findings.assertion: On 11 July 1692 the council recorded Sigüenza's delivery of rescued royal and viceregal portraits and books; Antonio de Ocaña and two colleagues were assigned a total of 18 pesos for helping save documents.
findings.exact_locator: edited cabildo abstract, PDF p.3, 11 July, 'ENTREGA DE ALHAJAS'
findings.limitations: Documentation from an abstract; precise identity and later whereabouts of objects not established.

findings.subject: New militia after the uprising
findings.assertion: Exbalin reports that on 9 June the viceroy organized a review of Spanish militia and subsequently two cavalry units and two Black and mulatto militia companies, while reforming the palace halberdiers.
findings.exact_locator: section 'Restoring order', paragraphs on 9 June military review and militia
findings.limitations: Different from claims of a modern standing police force; Exbalin characterizes the units as improvised.

findings.subject: Summary trial and punitive sentencing
findings.assertion: Exbalin reports an investigation launched 11 June; within twenty days about eighty accused people faced the Audiencia criminal chamber; twelve death sentences, thirty-two sentences of forced labor and flogging, and nine flogging-only sentences are reported.
findings.exact_locator: section 'Restoring order', paragraphs on judicial inquiry, penalties
findings.limitations: These figures are Exbalin's analysis of court materials, not an independent examination of case files; other defendants' dispositions not resolved.

findings.subject: Attempted ethnic segregation and its uncertain enforcement
findings.assertion: After the riot the viceregal government reissued restrictions on Indigenous residence inside the Spanish traza, granting a twenty-day departure period and threatening severe penalties; Exbalin explicitly states the actual degree of enforcement remains unknown.
findings.exact_locator: section 'Restoring order', paragraphs on delimiting traza and 20-day notice
themes: race law and urban social geography
findings.limitations: Edicts do not establish that Indigenous families were effectively expelled; never describe it as completed removal.

findings.subject: Pulque prohibition changed quickly
findings.assertion: Exbalin documents a pulque ban dated 19 July 1692, partial relaxation to medicinal white pulque on 31 July and renewed legalization in June 1697, connecting regulatory shifts partly to tax revenues and naval funding.
findings.exact_locator: section 'Restoring order', paragraphs on 19 and 31 July 1692 and June 1697
findings.limitations: This is legal policy chronology, not direct evidence of market enforcement or consumption patterns.

disputes.topic: Alleged death of a woman at alhóndiga
disputes.problem: Exbalin relates contemporary reports of a pregnant woman dying; Sigüenza claims women staged a death and even says a purported corpse moved. Neither suffices to establish her death or a hoax without reading competing testimonies; withhold from factual narrative.
